analysis.title: "The Asymmetry Has Shifted": Goldman Vol Trader Steps Off The AI Train With Hedge Funds The Most Crowded In Mag 7 On Record
key_insights: Goldman vol trader Shawn Tuteja (note titled 'a bit less clear') now says the Tech/AI upside asymmetry has shifted. On Aug 31 he called the risk-reward to owning upside 'extremely compelling' and recommended calls on Goldman's AI leaders basket. With the S&P at a record 7,818.93 and the Nasdaq 100 at a record 31,224, he no longer sees positioning in AI and large-cap tech as a tailwind.

Since Aug 27 the S&P 500 is up 1.28% while SPXXAI (S&P excluding AI names) is down 5.19%, a gap of about 6.5 points. The rolling 30-day SPX vs SPXXAI return gap is near its widest since January 2023. The same chart of NDX vs RTY tells a similar story.

Breadth is very narrow. In September the cap-weighted S&P beat the equal-weight index by about 4.5%, one of the widest monthly gaps in more than 25 years. Fewer than 25% of S&P members beat the index, the median stock is 17% below its all-time high, and the Nasdaq 100 outperformed the Russell 2000 on 14 of the last 16 sessions. BTIG's Krinsky cites a count of 14 'only seen in early 2000'.

Goldman's Financial Conditions Index has tightened about 40bps since end of June, almost entirely from long rates. The SOFR Dec-26/Dec-27 spread has steepened almost 50bps since end of August, which Tuteja reads as the market pricing more rate hikes through end of 2027. The Fed under Warsh hiked last month for the first time since July 2023, with the 10Y at 5.28% and the 30Y at 5.66%.

Goldman Prime Book: Mag 7 net exposure is near 22% of total US exposure, the highest on record in data going back to early 2022. Semis are about 12% of US exposure vs a June peak of 14% and about 6% at the start of the year. US Tech saw its largest percentage buying in a month since Feb 2025 in September and was the only sector net bought on the prime book.
Retail is also back: assets in US long levered semiconductor ETFs rebounded to about $115B from a trough of about $72B on July 29, still below the June peak.

Tuteja says the positioning numbers do not suggest AI positioning is near the June peak. They also no longer show tech and AI as under-owned or priced to pessimism on earnings cycle length. Just two companies are expected to deliver a third of all Q3 earnings growth.

Tuteja sees two paths. Either rates and oil turn friendlier and the index rises via broadening into other sectors, or the macro stays messy and large-cap tech and AI stall along with the market. He prefers broader market upside implementations over the AI ones favored in recent months.
Preferred trade: buy SPXXAI Nov 102% calls for 1.25%, described as a convex right-tail portfolio hedge should the macro become friendlier.

Floor argument: US Fundamental L/S net exposure is in the 2nd percentile on a 5-year lookback, and Pasquariello's discretionary length is 2 out of 10 on a -10 to 10 scale. Tuteja says clients would meaningfully add exposure around 7,400 in the S&P, about 5.4% below Tuesday's close.

Three reasons Tuteja expects dips in the broad index to be contained: 'uninvestable' pockets are cheap with low positioning, Fed speakers Williams, Jefferson and Bowman introduced a 'data-dependent' framework after Friday's 29K payrolls print that was below all estimates, and the midterms may clear the decks (S&P is normally flat from August to the midterm and fairly positive after).

Left-tail risk is CPI. The October meeting is priced at 5bps of hikes (vs a 64% chance of an October hike before Friday's jobs report). A high CPI forcing the Fed to hike would hurt all sectors near term, and the rest of 2027 would likely price much higher.

The AI Power basket (GSENEPOW) is the AI trade Tuteja still likes. Positioning is at the 15th percentile on a 3-year lookback, the forward P/E has fallen from about 26x to about 21x, and the basket rose about 5% Tuesday with Constellation (CEG) up 12% after Google plugged into Constellation's nuclear reactors. Trade: sell the 31-Dec 85% put to fund a 110%/135% call spread for 1.75%.
Options pricing around the Nov 3 midterms: an extra 1.69% implied election move in AI Power, more than 5x the 0.31% priced into the S&P and more than either party's policy basket.

Other desks: BTIG's Krinsky says lower yields could push QQQ and Mag7 lower, sees much greater downside risk to SPY/QQQ/Mag7, and says the SOX analog to 2000 holds. Morgan Stanley's Wilson says bad breadth must be resolved. Deutsche Bank's Allen says the bond market prices financial stress while equities do not, and that risk assets come under pressure unless stress eases. JPMorgan's trading desk flipped to Tactically Bullish last week.

Crowded Mag 7 positioning (record 22% of US exposure) and a rebound in levered semis ETF assets.
The Fed may need to hike an excessive number of times to maintain credibility in the back end of the curve.
Brent near $100 and 30Y at 5.66% pressure the macro backdrop.
Midterm outcome uncertainty, with the options market pricing it as largely an AI event.
Narrow breadth: a rally needs the rest of the index to participate.

tension_points.bull_case: Friendly rates and oil allow a broadening out, so SPXXAI and other sectors lead index upside. Hedge fund net exposure is at the 2nd percentile, so clients would buy dips near 7,400, and the midterms may clear the decks. JPMorgan's desk is Tactically Bullish.
tension_points.bear_case: The macro stays messy and AI and large-cap tech stall with the rest of the market. Mag 7 positioning is at a record, a hot CPI could force a Fed hike, and BTIG and Deutsche Bank warn of downside for the leaders.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A high CPI print forcing the Fed to hike at the October meeting (currently priced at 5bps) would open a left tail across all sectors.
